summary.intent: Run the GSD 'discuss' workflow for Phase 67 to identify and lock implementation decisions for the TEE lease-renewer contract rewrite, producing a CONTEXT.md that downstream researcher and planner agents can act on without re-asking the user.
summary.outcome: All four gray areas were discussed and locked, an adversarial verification workflow confirmed all 18 load-bearing code/spec claims against live source, and 67-CONTEXT.md + 67-DISCUSSION-LOG.md were written on a new feature branch.

repo: The TEE worker currently ORIGINATES fresh IPNS records from relay-supplied scalars rather than renewing existing ones — it is the inverse of the target lease-renewer contract.
Signing inputs come from ipns_republish_schedule rows (the snapshot), never from the canonical ipns_records row; ipns_records is only written back post-success.
The republish write-back uses LessThanOrEqual (forward-only UPDATE), not the equality CAS that the Phase-66 client publish path uses — the two paths are guarded differently.

The only tombstone check in the TEE renewal path (tombstonedAt: IsNull() in syncIpnsRecordSequence) runs AFTER delegated-routing publish — it prevents DB resurrection but not the signing or publishing itself.
Republish is driven by BullMQ (not a cron loop), so E2E tests can trigger a batch deterministically via queue.add() + a DB write setting nextRepublishAt to the past.
Local docker-compose does NOT start the tee-worker; it only runs in staging (docker-compose.staging.yml) and the production CVM config.
The tee-worker Vitest suite mocks the IPNS signer entirely, so no existing test exercises real record marshaling, EOL, or sequence behavior.

code.finding: The + 1n sequence increment and relay-supplied CID signing — the two behaviors §6.2 requires removing/relocating.
TEE_RECORD_LIFETIME_MS hardcoded to 48h; passed into createIpnsRecord at creation time; no extend-existing-record path exists anywhere.
teeEntries map reads all fields (encryptedIpnsKey, latestCid, sequenceNumber, keyEpoch) from the schedule batch entry; ipns_records is never queried to build the TEE request.
Write-back UPDATE uses sequenceNumber: LessThanOrEqual(newSequenceNumber) — forward-only, not equality CAS; tombstonedAt: IsNull() check here runs after publish.
Four columns duplicating ipns_records state: encrypted_ipns_key, key_epoch, latest_cid, sequence_number — these are the §6.3 columns to collapse.
Phase-66 equality CAS (WHERE sequence_number = :expected AND generation <= CAST(:incoming AS bigint) AND tombstoned_at IS NULL) exists only on the client publish path, not the TEE renewal path.
Encrypted key column is named encrypted_ipns_private_key here vs encrypted_ipns_key in the schedule entity — different names for the same duplicated datum.

workflow: Running an adversarial verification workflow before writing CONTEXT.md catches scout hallucinations early and lets the final document assert verified facts rather than single-source claims.
The GSD discuss workflow pattern: scout → discuss gray areas → adversarially verify load-bearing claims → write CONTEXT.md → commit on a new feature branch named after the phase.
Workflow output truncation is common for large verification passes; always read the full result from the output file path rather than relying on the truncated summary.

friction: Verification workflow output was truncated in the task notification, requiring a separate Read of the full output file to confirm the remaining clusters.

No local docker tee-worker makes it hard to develop/test the E2E path locally without modifying docker-compose — the enqueue surface and TEE_WORKER_URL wiring for local dev still need to be confirmed by the planner.

The spec's §7.1 noted renaming folder_ipns → ipns_records and dropping a public_key column, but the entity already uses ipns_records and has no public_key column — cross-checking whether that rename is fully done or partially done required extra grep work.
open_items: Planner research flag: confirm the exact enqueue surface in republish.module.ts (is there a @Cron / repeatable BullMQ job, and does the test trigger via queue.add vs a dev endpoint vs direct processRepublishBatch()), and confirm local-compose TEE_WORKER_URL wiring.
Pre-publish tombstone gate must be added to the TEE/relay path — the existing guard only protects the DB write-back, not the signing or delegated-routing publish.
Migration required to collapse the 4 duplicated columns from ipns_republish_schedule (encrypted_ipns_key, key_epoch, latest_cid, sequence_number) and make ipns_records the sole signing-input source.
TEE internal epoch derivation from the enclave's own clock/schedule (never trusting relay-supplied currentEpoch) — design not yet specified precisely enough for implementation.
Client re-enrollment recovery path (§6.7-item-3 migration durability) deliberately deferred — TEE signing contract must be correct first.

sdk-e2e round-trip tests for §7.3 scenarios: test 12 (stale-CID, revoked CID never re-signed), test 17 (renewal racing a forward publish), test 18 (name↔key binding), test 19 (TEE epoch self-derivation), test 20 (tombstoned name rejection) — none exist today.
